title: Gate test (deliberately bad): only pronouns make a claim Context-dependent
target_rule_text_at_authoring: A definite reference that needs an outside antecedent to identify it ("the vulnerabilities", "the discussions", "the recording", "the settlement terms", "the legal dispute", "recent actions") makes the claim Context-dependent, even when other entities in the claim are named.
proposed_text: Only a pronoun without an antecedent inside the claim makes it Context-dependent; a definite description never does if the sentence reads well on its own.
statement: Editors decided that a claim which reads well on its own is not Context-dependent, even when it contains a definite phrase ('Georgia's gubernatorial debate', 'the larger public health problem'). The rule should say so in general: only a pronoun with no antecedent inside the claim makes a claim Context-dependent, and a definite description never does when the sentence reads well on its own.

boundary_examples.claim: He said the plan would fail.
The ruling on the new tariff schedule was announced yesterday.

note: A planted test, not a real lesson, and expected to FAIL the gate. It rewrites rule 2 of Context-dependent so that only a bare pronoun counts. That over-generalises the two real decisions behind it (Georgia, COVID) and contradicts the tag's own example claims ('the target group', 'the launch', 'the vulnerabilities', 'the discussions', 'the Bitcoin ETF') and rules 3 and 4, so the canaries of Context-dependent and of its counterpart Self-contained are expected to fail. After a FAIL the Rulebook stays untouched and the lesson ends Rolled back.
